author: Tarheelkiwi
body:
I was looking at the infractions page and I noticed that in the last 6 pages (I gave up after that) none of the staff members used /warn.  They all used /kick instead.  Also, what is the point of /warn when you can verbally warn the in chat and it is just as affective.  So I was thinking, why don't we just remove /warn because it is proving to be pointless.

Tell me what you guys think.


-Tarheelkiwi

replies.author: SnowSX3
replies.body:
/warn is currently broken as it doesn't show up for the player in-game. It only shows up on the website which completely negates the purpose of /warn.

This issue is getting fixed and in the meantime, Moderators give out 1 or 2 verbal warnings and then kick the player in question.

replies.author: SnowSX3
replies.body:
Some players don't listen to verbal warnings.

So when dealing with a minor offence, /warn is a good way to officially warn the player that they need to stop what they're doing negatively.

replies.author: Pelpelajax
replies.body: /warn is broken. If we were to just use a verbal warn the punishment would never be recorded. Therefor there is no evidence that it has been given. It is a useful tool for us to see what punishment a player should receive next.
replies.body_tagged: /warn is broken. If we were to just use a verbal warn the punishment would never be recorded. Therefor there is no evidence that it has been given. It is a useful tool for us to see what punishment a player should receive next.

replies.author: IviFetita
replies.body: Also, '/warn' is added to the player's infractions tab, so it'd be fair for people or staff who want to see the player's infractions... in staff applications if you got warned 100 times verbally for say in the chat 'F*** you!'; the staff couldn't see it and he could get banned after all the non-registered infractions.
